+            end = text.find(ch, i + 1)

+            nl = text.find("\n", i + 1)

+            if end == -1 or (nl != -1 and nl < end):

+                raise DslError("line %d: unterminated string literal" % line)

+            if start_line is None:

+                start_line = line

+            current.append(text[i:end + 1])

+            i = end + 1

+            continue

+        if ch == "#":

+            nl = text.find("\n", i)

+            i = n if nl == -1 else nl

+            continue

+        if ch == "\r":

+            i += 1

+            continue

+        if ch == "\n":

+            line += 1

+            i += 1

+            so_far = "".join(current).strip()

+            if not so_far:

+                continue

+            if depth > 0 or so_far.endswith(","):

+                current.append(" ")

+                continue

+            if _next_significant_char(text, i) == ",":

+                current.append(" ")

+                continue

+            flush()

+            start_line = None

+            depth = 0

+            continue

+        if ch in "{}" and depth <= 0:

+            flush()

+            statements.append((line, ch))

+            start_line = None

+            depth = 0

+            i += 1

+            continue

+        if ch in "([":

+            depth += 1

+        elif ch in ")]":

+            depth -= 1

+        if start_line is None and not ch.isspace():

+            start_line = line

+        current.append(ch)

+        i += 1

+    flush()

+    return statements

+

+

+def _next_significant_char(text, i):

+    n = len(text)

+    while i < n:

+        ch = text[i]

+        if ch.isspace():

+            i += 1

+        elif ch == "#":

+            nl = text.find("\n", i)

+            if nl == -1:

+                return None

+            i = nl

+        else:

+            return ch

+    return None

+

+

+def _tokenize(stmt, line):

+    tokens = []

+    pos = 0

+    while pos < len(stmt):

+        m = _TOKEN_RE.match(stmt, pos)

+        if not m:

+            raise DslError("line %d: unexpected character %r" % (line, stmt[pos]))

+        kind = m.lastgroup

+        if kind != "ws":

+            tokens.append(_Token(kind, m.group(), pos))

+        pos = m.end()

+    tokens.append(_Token("eof", "", pos))

+    return tokens

+

+

+class _StatementParser:

+    def __init__(self, stmt, line):

+        self.line = line

+        self.stmt = stmt

+        self.tokens = _tokenize(stmt, line)

+        self.i = 0

+

+    # -- token helpers -------------------------------------------------

+    def peek(self, offset=0):

+        return self.tokens[min(self.i + offset, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

+

+    def advance(self):

+        tok = self.tokens[self.i]

+        if tok.kind != "eof":

+            self.i += 1

+        return tok

+

+    def fail(self, message, tok=None):

+        tok = tok or self.peek()

+        where = "end of statement" if tok.kind == "eof" else repr(tok.text)

+        raise DslError("line %d: %s (at %s)" % (self.line, message, where))

+

+    def is_op(self, text):

+        tok = self.peek()

+        return tok.kind == "op" and tok.text == text

+

+    def is_word(self, text):

+        tok = self.peek()

+        return tok.kind == "ident" and tok.text == text

+

+    def expect_op(self, text):

+        if not self.is_op(text):

+            self.fail("expected %r" % text)

+        return self.advance()

+

+    def expect_word(self, text):

+        if not self.is_word(text):

+            self.fail("expected %r" % text)

+        return self.advance()

+

+    def expect_ident(self, what):

+        tok = self.peek()

+        if tok.kind != "ident":

+            self.fail("expected %s" % what)

+        return self.advance().text

+

+    def expect_end(self):

+        if self.peek().kind != "eof":

+            self.fail("unexpected trailing input")

+

+    def type_name(self):

+        tok = self.peek()

+        name = self.expect_ident("a type name")

+        if name not in TYPE_NAMES:

+            self.fail("unknown type %r" % name, tok)

+        return name

+

+    # -- block headers and declarations --------------------------------

+    def schema_header(self):

+        self.expect_word("schema")

+        name = self.expect_ident("a schema name")

+        base = None

+        if self.is_word("extends"):

+            self.advance()

+            base = self.expect_ident("a base schema name")

+            if self.is_op(","):

+                self.fail("multiple inheritance is not allowed")

+        self.expect_end()

+        return name, base

+

+    def pipeline_header(self):

+        self.expect_word("pipeline")

+        name = self.expect_ident("a pipeline name")

+        schema = None

+        if not self.is_op("{") and self.peek().kind != "eof":

+            self.expect_word("using")

+            schema = self.expect_ident("a schema name")

+        self.expect_end()

+        return name, schema

+

+    # -- multi-source constructs ---------------------------------------

+    def source_bindings(self):

+        """name [as alias] {, name [as alias]}  (a trailing comma is allowed)"""

+        bindings = []

+        while self.peek().kind != "eof":

+            name = self.expect_ident("a source name")

+            alias = name

+            if self.is_word("as"):

+                self.advance()

+                alias = self.expect_ident("a source alias")

+            if alias == WORKING_RELATION:

+                self.fail("%r is reserved for the working relation" % WORKING_RELATION)

+            bindings.append(P.SourceBinding(name, alias))

+            if not self.is_op(","):

+                break

+            self.advance()

+        self.expect_end()

+        return bindings

+

+    def with_header(self):

+        self.expect_word("with")

+        alias = self.expect_ident("a source alias")

+        self.expect_end()

+        return alias

+

+    def join_header(self):

+        """join <left> with <right> on (<expr>) [within <duration>] [type <kind>] project"""

+        self.expect_word("join")

+        left = self.join_operand()

+        self.expect_word("with")

+        right = self.join_operand()

+        on = within = kind = None

+        while not self.is_word("project"):

+            tok = self.peek()

+            if tok.kind == "eof":

+                raise DslError("line %d: join requires a project { ... } clause" % self.line)

+            if self.is_word("on") and on is None:

+                self.advance()

+                on = self.expression()

+            elif self.is_word("within") and within is None:

+                self.advance()

+                within = self.duration()

+            elif self.is_word("type") and kind is None:

+                self.advance()

+                tok = self.peek()

+                kind = self.expect_ident("a join type")

+                if kind not in JOIN_TYPES:

+                    self.fail("unknown join type %r (expected inner, left, right or full)"

+                              % kind, tok)

+            else:

+                self.fail("expected on, within, type or project in join")

+        self.advance()

+        self.expect_end()

+        if on is None:

+            raise DslError("line %d: join requires an on (...) predicate" % self.line)

+        return left, right, on, within, kind or "inner"

+

+    def join_operand(self):

+        return self.expect_ident("a source alias, join alias or _")

+

+    def duration(self):

+        if self.is_word("param") and self.peek(1).kind == "op" and self.peek(1).text == "(":

+            self.advance()

+            return P.Duration(None, None, self.param_ref().name)

+        tok = self.peek()

+        if tok.kind != "int":

+            self.fail("expected a duration such as 10m")

+        self.advance()

+        amount = int(tok.text)

+        unit_tok = self.peek()

+        unit = self.expect_ident("a duration unit (s, m, h or d)")

+        if unit not in _DURATION_UNITS:

+            self.fail("unknown duration unit %r" % unit, unit_tok)

+        if unit_tok.pos != tok.pos + len(tok.text):

+            self.fail("expected a duration such as 10m", unit_tok)

+        return P.Duration(amount, unit, None)

+

+    def project_items(self):

+        """<expr> [as <name>] {, ...}; a bare column reference keeps its column name."""

+        items = []

+        while self.peek().kind != "eof":

+            start = self.peek()

+            expr = self.expression()

+            if self.is_word("as"):

+                self.advance()

+                tok = self.peek()

+                if tok.kind == "string" and len(tok.text) > 2:

+                    name = self.advance().text[1:-1]

+                else:

+                    name = self.expect_ident("a projected column name")

+            elif isinstance(expr, P.ColumnRef):

+                name = expr.name.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]

+            else:

+                self.fail("project entries need 'as <name>'", start)

+            items.append(P.ProjectItem(expr, name))

+            if not self.is_op(","):

+                break

+            self.advance()

+        self.expect_end()

+        return items

+

+    def join_alias(self):

+        self.expect_word("as")

+        alias = self.expect_ident("a join alias")

+        self.expect_end()

+        return alias

+

+    def field_list(self):

+        """name: type [= expr] {, name: type [= expr]}"""

+        fields = [self.field()]

+        while self.is_op(","):

+            self.advance()

+            fields.append(self.field())

+        self.expect_end()

+        return fields

+

+    def field(self):

+        name = self.expect_ident("a field name")

+        self.expect_op(":")

+        value_type = self.type_name()

+        expr = None

+        if self.is_op("="):

+            self.advance()

+            expr = self.expression()

+        return P.FieldDef(name, value_type, expr)

+

+    def param_list(self):

+        """name [: type] [= literal] {, ...}"""

+        params = [self.param_decl()]

+        while self.is_op(","):

+            self.advance()

+            params.append(self.param_decl())

+        self.expect_end()

+        return params

+

+    def param_decl(self):

+        name = self.expect_ident("a parameter name")

+        value_type = default = None

+        if self.is_op(":"):

+            self.advance()

+            value_type = self.type_name()

+        if self.is_op("="):

+            self.advance()

+            default = self.literal()

+        return P.ParamDef(name, value_type, default)

+

+    def literal(self):

+        sign = None

+        if self.peek().kind == "op" and self.peek().text in ("-", "+"):

+            sign = self.advance().text

+        tok = self.peek()

+        if tok.kind in ("int", "float"):

+            self.advance()

+            value = int(tok.text) if tok.kind == "int" else float(tok.text)

+            return P.Literal(tok.kind, -value if sign == "-" else value)

+        if sign is None:

+            if tok.kind == "string":

+                self.advance()

+                return P.Literal("string", tok.text[1:-1])

+            if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.text in ("true", "false"):

+                self.advance()

+                return P.Literal("bool", tok.text == "true")

+        self.fail("expected a literal value")

+

+    # -- statements ----------------------------------------------------

+    def statement(self):

+        keyword = self.peek()

+        if keyword.kind != "ident":

+            self.fail("expected a statement keyword")

+        name = keyword.text

+        if name == "filter":

+            return self.filter_statement()

+        if name == "apply":

+            return self.apply_statement()

+        if name == "group_by":

+            return self.group_by_statement()

+        if name == "window":

+            return self.window_statement()

+        if name == "aggregate":

+            return self.aggregate_statement()

+        if name == "calc":

+            return self.calc_statement()

+        self.fail("unknown statement %r" % name, keyword)

+

+    def filter_statement(self):

+        self.advance()

+        self.expect_op("(")

+        expr = self.expression()

+        self.expect_op(")")

+        self.expect_end()

+        return P.Filter(expr)

+

+    def apply_statement(self):

+        self.advance()

+        self.expect_op("(")

+        expr = self.expression()

+        self.expect_op(",")

+        tok = self.peek()

+        if tok.kind == "ident":

+            column = self.advance().text

+        elif tok.kind == "string" and len(tok.text) > 2:

+            column = self.advance().text[1:-1]

+        else:

+            self.fail("expected a new column name")

+        self.expect_op(")")

+        self.expect_end()

+        return P.Apply(expr, column)

+

+    def group_by_statement(self):

+        self.advance()

+        self.expect_op("(")

+        bracketed = self.is_op("[")

+        if bracketed:

+            self.advance()

+        columns = [self.group_column()]

+        while self.is_op(","):

+            self.advance()

+            columns.append(self.group_column())

+        if bracketed:

+            self.expect_op("]")

+        self.expect_op(")")

+        self.expect_end()

+        if len(set(columns)) != len(columns):

+            raise DslError("line %d: duplicate column in group_by" % self.line)

+        return P.GroupBy(tuple(columns))

+

+    def group_column(self):

+        tok = self.peek()

+        if tok.kind == "string" and len(tok.text) > 2:

+            return self.advance().text[1:-1]

+        return self.expect_ident("a column name")

+

+    def window_statement(self):

+        m = re.match(r"^window\s*\(\s*(\d+)([mhd])\s*\)$", self.stmt)

+        if m:

+            amount = int(m.group(1))

+            if amount <= 0:

+                raise DslError("line %d: window duration must be positive" % self.line)

+            return P.Window(amount, m.group(2))

+        self.advance()

+        self.expect_op("(")

+        if self.is_word("param") and self.peek(1).kind == "op" and self.peek(1).text == "(":

+            self.advance()

+            ref = self.param_ref()

+            self.expect_op(")")

+            self.expect_end()

+            return P.Window(None, None, ref.name)

+        raise DslError("line %d: invalid window statement, expected window(<n><m|h|d>)"

+                       % self.line)

+

+    def aggregate_statement(self):

+        self.advance()

+        items = [self.aggregate_item()]

+        while self.is_op(","):

+            self.advance()

+            items.append(self.aggregate_item())

+        self.expect_end()

+        aliases = [it.alias for it in items]

+        if len(set(aliases)) != len(aliases):

+            raise DslError("line %d: aggregate aliases must be unique" % self.line)

+        return P.Aggregate(tuple(items))

+

+    def aggregate_item(self):

+        fn_tok = self.peek()

+        fn = self.expect_ident("an aggregate function")

+        if fn not in AGGREGATE_FUNCTIONS:

+            self.fail("unknown aggregate function %r" % fn, fn_tok)

+        self.expect_op("(")

+        if self.is_op("*"):

+            self.advance()

+            column = None

+        else:

+            column = self.expect_ident("a column name or *")

+        self.expect_op(")")

+        self.expect_word("as")

+        alias = self.expect_ident("an alias")

+        return P.AggregateItem(fn, column, alias)

+

+    def calc_statement(self):

+        """calc name = expr : type [@stage(pre|post_agg)]  (or calc name: type = expr ...)"""

+        self.advance()

+        name = self.expect_ident("a calculated field name")

+        if self.is_op(":"):

+            self.advance()

+            value_type = self.type_name()

+            self.expect_op("=")

+            expr = self.expression()

+        else:

+            self.expect_op("=")

+            expr = self.expression()

+            self.expect_op(":")

+            value_type = self.type_name()

+        stage = P.STAGE_PRE

+        if self.is_op("@"):

+            self.advance()

+            self.expect_word("stage")

+            self.expect_op("(")

+            tok = self.peek()

+            stage = self.expect_ident("a stage name")

+            if stage not in _STAGES:

+                self.fail("unknown stage %r (expected pre or post_agg)" % stage, tok)

+            self.expect_op(")")

+        self.expect_end()

+        return P.Calc(name, expr, value_type, stage)

+

+    # -- expressions ---------------------------------------------------

+    def expression(self):

+        return self.or_expr()

+

+    def or_expr(self):

+        left = self.and_expr()

+        while self.is_op("|"):

+            self.advance()

+            left = P.Binary("|", left, self.and_expr())

+        return left

+

+    def and_expr(self):

+        left = self.not_expr()

+        while self.is_op("&"):

+            self.advance()

+            left = P.Binary("&", left, self.not_expr())

+        return left

+

+    def not_expr(self):

+        if self.is_op("!"):

+            self.advance()

+            return P.Unary("!", self.not_expr())

+        return self.comparison()

+

+    def comparison(self):

+        left = self.additive()

+        tok = self.peek()

+        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.text in ("<", "<=", ">", ">=", "==", "!="):

+            op = self.advance().text

+            right = self.additive()

+            self.reject_chain()

+            return P.Binary(op, left, right)

+        if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.text == "in":

+            self.advance()

+            right = self.additive()

+            self.reject_chain()

+            return P.Binary("in", left, right)

+        if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.text in _STRING_OPS:

+            op = self.advance().text

+            right = self.additive()

+            self.reject_chain()

+            return P.Call(op, (left, right))

+        return left

+

+    def reject_chain(self):

+        tok = self.peek()

+        if (tok.kind == "op" and tok.text in ("<", "<=", ">", ">=", "==", "!=")) or \

+                (tok.kind == "ident" and tok.text in ("in",) + _STRING_OPS):

+            self.fail("comparisons cannot be chained")

+

+    def additive(self):

+        left = self.term()

+        while self.peek().kind == "op" and self.peek().text in ("+", "-"):

+            op = self.advance().text

+            left = P.Binary(op, left, self.term())

+        return left

+

+    def term(self):

+        left = self.unary()

+        while self.peek().kind == "op" and self.peek().text in ("*", "/", "%"):

+            op = self.advance().text

+            left = P.Binary(op, left, self.unary())

+        return left

+

+    def unary(self):

+        if self.peek().kind == "op" and self.peek().text in ("-", "+"):

+            op = self.advance().text

+            return P.Unary(op, self.unary())

+        return self.primary()

+

+    def primary(self):

+        tok = self.peek()

+        if tok.kind == "int":

+            self.advance()

+            return P.Literal("int", int(tok.text))

+        if tok.kind == "float":

+            self.advance()

+            return P.Literal("float", float(tok.text))

+        if tok.kind == "string":

+            self.advance()

+            return P.Literal("string", tok.text[1:-1])

+        if tok.kind == "ident":

+            if tok.text in ("true", "false"):

+                self.advance()

+                return P.Literal("bool", tok.text == "true")

+            if tok.text in ("in", "as"):

+                self.fail("unexpected keyword")

+            self.advance()

+            if self.is_op(".") and self.peek(1).kind == "ident":

+                self.advance()

+                return P.ColumnRef("%s.%s" % (tok.text, self.advance().text))

+            if self.is_op("("):

+                if tok.text == "param":

+                    return self.param_ref()

+                if tok.text == "cast":

+                    return self.cast()

+                return self.call(tok)

+            return P.ColumnRef(tok.text)

+        if self.is_op("("):

+            self.advance()

+            inner = self.expression()

+            self.expect_op(")")

+            return inner

+        self.fail("expected an expression")

+

+    def param_ref(self):

+        self.expect_op("(")

+        tok = self.peek()

+        if tok.kind != "string" or len(tok.text) <= 2:

+            self.fail("param() expects a quoted parameter name")

+        self.advance()

+        self.expect_op(")")

+        return P.Param(tok.text[1:-1])

+

+    def cast(self):

+        self.expect_op("(")

+        inner = self.expression()

+        self.expect_word("as")

+        value_type = self.type_name()

+        self.expect_op(")")

+        return P.Cast(inner, value_type)

+

+    def call(self, tok):

+        self.expect_op("(")

+        args = []

+        if not self.is_op(")"):

+            args.append(self.expression())

+            while self.is_op(","):

+                self.advance()

+                args.append(self.expression())

+        self.expect_op(")")

+        if tok.text not in _TRANSFORM_ARITY:

+            # Possibly a user-defined function; parse_program checks the name.

+            return P.Call(tok.text, tuple(args))

+        low, high = _TRANSFORM_ARITY[tok.text]

+        if len(args) < low or (high is not None and len(args) > high):

+            self.fail("wrong number of arguments to %s()" % tok.text, tok)

+        return P.Call(tok.text, tuple(args))

+

+

+def _first_word(stmt):

+    m = re.match(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*", stmt)

+    return m.group() if m else None

+

+def parse_program(text, functions=None):

+    """Parse DSL source into a program.Program; raises DslError.

+

+    functions: name -> arity of the registered user-defined functions.

+    """

+    statements = _logical_lines(text)

+    if any(stmt in ("{", "}") or _first_word(stmt) in ("schema", "pipeline")

+           for _, stmt in statements):

+        program = _parse_blocks(statements)

+    else:

+        program = _build_program(statements)

+    _check_functions(program, functions or {})

+    return program

+

+

+def is_builtin_function(name):

+    return name in _TRANSFORM_ARITY

+

+

+def _check_functions(program, functions):

+    for top in P.program_expressions(program):

+        for node in P.walk(top):

+            if not isinstance(node, P.Call) or node.name in _TRANSFORM_ARITY:

+                continue

+            if node.name not in functions:

+                raise DslError("unknown function %r" % node.name)

+            if len(node.args) != functions[node.name]:

+                raise DslError("wrong number of arguments to %s(): expected %d, got %d"

+                               % (node.name, functions[node.name], len(node.args)))

+

+

+def _build_program(statements, **extra):

+    steps = []

+    calcs = []

+    group_by = window = aggregate = None

+    for line, stmt in statements:

+        node = _StatementParser(stmt, line).statement()

+        if isinstance(node, (P.Filter, P.Apply)):

+            steps.append(node)

+        elif isinstance(node, P.Calc):

+            calcs.append(node)

+        elif isinstance(node, P.GroupBy):

+            if group_by is not None:

+                raise DslError("line %d: group_by may appear at most once" % line)

+            group_by = node

+        elif isinstance(node, P.Window):

+            if window is not None:

+                raise DslError("line %d: window may appear at most once" % line)

+            window = node

+        else:

+            if aggregate is not None:

+                raise DslError("line %d: aggregate must appear exactly once" % line)

+            aggregate = node

+    if aggregate is None:

+        raise DslError("program has no aggregate statement")

+    _check_calc_names(calcs)

+    _check_output_names(group_by, window, aggregate, calcs)

+    return P.Program(steps, group_by, window, aggregate, calcs=calcs, **extra)

+        self.i = 0

+

+    def done(self):

+        return self.i >= len(self.statements)

+

+    def next(self, what):

+        if self.done():

+            raise DslError("unexpected end of DSL: expected %s" % what)

+        item = self.statements[self.i]

+        self.i += 1

+        return item

+

+    def expect_open(self, what):

+        line, stmt = self.next("'{' after %s header" % what)

+        if stmt != "{":

+            raise DslError("line %d: expected '{' after %s header" % (line, what))

+

+    def block(self, what):

+        """Yield (line, stmt) up to the closing brace of the current block."""

+        while True:

+            line, stmt = self.next("'}' closing %s block" % what)

+            if stmt == "}":

+                return

+            if stmt == "{":

+                raise DslError("line %d: unexpected '{' in %s block" % (line, what))

+            yield line, stmt

+

+

+def _parse_blocks(statements):

+    cursor = _Cursor(statements)

+    schemas = {}

+    pipeline = None

+    while not cursor.done():

+        line, stmt = cursor.next("a block")

+        word = _first_word(stmt)

+        if word == "schema":

+            name, base = _StatementParser(stmt, line).schema_header()

+            if name in schemas:

+                raise DslError("line %d: schema %r is defined more than once" % (line, name))

+            cursor.expect_open("schema")

+            fields = []

+            seen = set()

+            for fline, fstmt in cursor.block("schema"):

+                for field in _StatementParser(fstmt, fline).field_list():

+                    if field.name in seen:

+                        raise DslError("line %d: field %r declared twice in schema %r"

+                                       % (fline, field.name, name))

+                    seen.add(field.name)

+                    fields.append(field)

+            schemas[name] = P.SchemaDef(name, base, tuple(fields))

+        elif word == "pipeline":

+            if pipeline is not None:

+                raise DslError("line %d: only one pipeline block is allowed" % line)

+            pipeline = (line,) + _StatementParser(stmt, line).pipeline_header()

+            cursor.expect_open("pipeline")

+            pipeline += _pipeline_body(cursor)

+        else:

+            raise DslError("line %d: expected a schema or pipeline block" % line)

+    if pipeline is None:

+        raise DslError("DSL has no pipeline block")

+    line, name, schema_name, body, params, sources, scoped, joins = pipeline

+    if schema_name is None:

+        if sources is None:

+            raise DslError("line %d: pipeline requires 'using <schema>'" % line)

+    elif schema_name not in schemas:

+        raise DslError("line %d: pipeline uses unknown schema %r" % (line, schema_name))

+    _check_sources(sources, scoped, joins)

+    return _build_program(body, params=params, schemas=schemas,

+                          schema_name=schema_name, name=name, sources=sources,

+                          scoped=scoped, joins=joins)

+

+

+def _pipeline_body(cursor):

+    body = []

+    params = None

+    sources = None

+    scoped = []

+    joins = []

+    started = False

+    while True:

+        line, stmt = cursor.next("'}' closing pipeline block")

+        if stmt == "}":

+            break

+        if stmt == "{":

+            raise DslError("line %d: unexpected '{' in pipeline block" % line)

+        word = _first_word(stmt)

+        if word == "sources" and stmt.strip() == "sources":

+            if sources is not None:

+                raise DslError("line %d: sources block may appear at most once" % line)

+            if started:

+                raise DslError("line %d: sources block must precede all other statements"

+                               % line)

+            cursor.expect_open("sources")

+            sources = []

+            for bline, bstmt in cursor.block("sources"):

+                sources.extend(_StatementParser(bstmt, bline).source_bindings())

+            if not sources:

+                raise DslError("line %d: sources block binds no source" % line)

+            started = True

+            continue

+        if word == "with":

+            scoped.append(_scoped_block(cursor, line, stmt))

+            started = True

+            continue

+        if word == "join":

+            joins.append(_join(cursor, line, stmt))

+            started = True

+            continue

+        if word == "params" and stmt.strip() == "params":

+            if params is not None:

+                raise DslError("line %d: params block may appear at most once" % line)

+            cursor.expect_open("params")

+            params = []

+            seen = set()

+            for pline, pstmt in cursor.block("params"):

+                for decl in _StatementParser(pstmt, pline).param_list():

+                    if decl.name in seen:

+                        raise DslError("line %d: parameter %r declared twice"

+                                       % (pline, decl.name))

+                    seen.add(decl.name)

+                    params.append(decl)

+        else:

+            body.append((line, stmt))

+            started = True

+    return body, tuple(params or ()), sources, scoped, joins

+

+

+def _scoped_block(cursor, line, stmt):

+    alias = _StatementParser(stmt, line).with_header()

+    cursor.expect_open("with")

+    steps = []

+    for sline, sstmt in cursor.block("with"):

+        node = _StatementParser(sstmt, sline).statement()

+        if isinstance(node, (P.GroupBy, P.Window, P.Aggregate)):

+            raise DslError("line %d: with %s { } accepts only pre-stage calcs and filters"

+                           % (sline, alias))

+        if isinstance(node, P.Calc) and node.stage != P.STAGE_PRE:

+            raise TypeCheckError("line %d: calc %r: @stage(%s) is not allowed inside with %s { }"

+                                 % (sline, node.name, node.stage, alias))

+        steps.append(node)

+    return P.ScopedBlock(alias, tuple(steps), line)

+

+

+def _join(cursor, line, stmt):

+    parts = [stmt]

+    while not re.search(r"\bproject\s*$", parts[-1]) and not cursor.done():

+        nstmt = cursor.statements[cursor.i][1]

+        if _first_word(nstmt) not in _JOIN_CLAUSES:

+            break

+        cursor.i += 1

+        parts.append(nstmt)

+    header = " ".join(parts)

+    left, right, on, within, kind = _StatementParser(header, line).join_header()

+    if cursor.done() or cursor.statements[cursor.i][1] != "{":

+        raise DslError("line %d: expected '{' after project" % line)

+    cursor.i += 1

+    items = []

+    for pline, pstmt in cursor.block("project"):

+        items.extend(_StatementParser(pstmt, pline).project_items())

+    if not items:

+        raise DslError("line %d: project { } must define at least one column" % line)

+    names = [item.name for item in items]

+    for name in names:

+        if names.count(name) > 1:

+            raise DslError("line %d: column %r appears more than once in project; "

+                           "disambiguate it with 'as'" % (line, name))

+    alias = None

+    if not cursor.done() and _first_word(cursor.statements[cursor.i][1]) == "as":

+        aline, astmt = cursor.next("a join alias")

+        alias = _StatementParser(astmt, aline).join_alias()

+    return P.Join(left, right, on, within, kind, tuple(items), alias, line)

+

+

+def _check_sources(sources, scoped, joins):

+    if sources is None:

+        if joins:

+            raise DslError("line %d: join requires a sources { } block" % joins[0].line)

+        if scoped:

+            raise DslError("line %d: with blocks require a sources { } block" % scoped[0].line)

+        return

+    aliases = set()

+    for binding in sources:

+        if binding.alias in aliases:

+            raise DslError("source alias %r is bound more than once" % binding.alias)

+        aliases.add(binding.alias)

+    if not joins:

+        raise DslError("pipeline declares sources but no join combines them")

+    for block in scoped:

+        if block.alias not in aliases:

+            raise DslError("line %d: with refers to unknown source alias %r"

+                           % (block.line, block.alias))

+    known = set(aliases)

+    for index, join in enumerate(joins):

+        for operand in (join.left, join.right):

+            if operand == WORKING_RELATION:

+                if index == 0:

+                    raise DslError("line %d: '_' refers to the previous join, but this is the "

+                                   "first join" % join.line)

+            elif operand not in known:

+                raise DslError("line %d: join refers to unknown alias %r" % (join.line, operand))

+        if join.left == join.right:

+            raise DslError("line %d: cannot join %r with itself; bind the source twice under "

+                           "different aliases" % (join.line, join.left))

+        if join.alias is not None:

+            if join.alias in known or join.alias == WORKING_RELATION:

+                raise DslError("line %d: join alias %r is already in use"

+                               % (join.line, join.alias))

+            known.add(join.alias)

+

+

+def _check_calc_names(calcs):

+    seen = set()

+    for calc in calcs:

+        if calc.name in seen:

+            raise DslError("calculated field %r is declared more than once" % calc.name)

+        seen.add(calc.name)

+

+

+def _check_output_names(group_by, window, aggregate, calcs):

+    taken = set(group_by.columns) if group_by else set()

+    if window:

+        clash = taken.intersection(_RESERVED_OUTPUT)

+        if clash:

+            raise DslError("group_by column %r collides with a window field" % sorted(clash)[0])

+        taken.update(_RESERVED_OUTPUT)

+    for item in aggregate.items:

+        if item.alias in taken:

+            raise DslError("aggregate alias %r collides with another output field" % item.alias)

+        taken.add(item.alias)

+    for calc in calcs:

+        if calc.stage == P.STAGE_POST and calc.name in taken:

+            raise DslError("calculated field %r collides with another output field" % calc.name)

+"""DSL versions.

+

+Secret: the shape of the `mtl_version` header, which language version

+introduced each construct, the compatibility rules (unsupported majors,

+higher minors, constructs newer than the declared version) and when an

+older declared version earns a warning.

+"""

+

+import re

+from collections import namedtuple

+

+from . import program as P

+from .dsl_parser import is_builtin_function

+from .errors import ArtifactError, DslError

+

+RUNTIME_VERSION = "1.5.0"

+

+Version = namedtuple("Version", "major minor")

+Version.__str__ = lambda v: "%d.%d" % v

+

+SUPPORTED = Version(1, 5)

+_PART5 = Version(1, 5)

+

+_HEADER_WORD = re.compile(r"^\s*mtl_version(?![A-Za-z0-9_])")

+_HEADER = re.compile(r"^\s*mtl_version[ \t]+(\d+)\.(\d+)[ \t]*(#.*)?$")

+

+

+def read_header(text):

+    """(declared Version, DSL text with the header line blanked out).

+

+    The header must be the first line that is neither blank nor a comment.

+    """

+    lines = text.split("\n")

+    for index, line in enumerate(lines):

+        stripped = line.strip()

+        if not stripped or stripped.startswith("#"):

+            continue

+        if not _HEADER_WORD.match(line):

+            raise ArtifactError("line %d: missing version header; the DSL must start with "

+                                "'mtl_version <major>.<minor>'" % (index + 1))

+        m = _HEADER.match(line.rstrip("\r"))

+        if not m:

+            raise DslError("line %d: invalid version header, expected "

+                           "'mtl_version <major>.<minor>'" % (index + 1))

+        version = Version(int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)))

+        if version.major != SUPPORTED.major:

+            raise ArtifactError("unsupported mtl_version %s: this runtime supports %d.x "

+                                "(up to %s)" % (version, SUPPORTED.major, SUPPORTED))

+        lines[index] = ""

+        return version, "\n".join(lines)

+    raise ArtifactError("missing version header; the DSL must start with "

+                        "'mtl_version <major>.<minor>'")

+

+

+def check_features(program, declared):

+    """Raise DslError if the program uses a construct newer than `declared`."""

+    newest = None

+    for needed, what in _features(program):

+        if needed > declared and (newest is None or needed > newest[0]):

+            newest = (needed, what)

+    if newest is not None:

+        raise DslError("%s requires mtl_version %s or later, but the DSL declares %s"

+                       % (newest[1], newest[0], declared))

+

+

+def warning(declared, uses_part5):

+    """One-line warning text for an older declared minor version, or None."""

+    if declared >= SUPPORTED:

+        return None

+    message = ("DSL declares mtl_version %s, older than this runtime's %s; constructs are "

+               "gated at %s but runtime semantics are those of %s" % (declared, SUPPORTED,

+                                                                     declared, SUPPORTED))

+    if uses_part5 and declared < _PART5:

+        message += "; resumable state and run metadata are mtl_version %s features" % _PART5

+    return message

+

+

+def _features(program):

+    """(minimum Version, description) of each versioned construct the program uses."""

+    v12, v13, v14 = Version(1, 2), Version(1, 3), Version(1, 4)

+    if program.joins:

+        yield v14, "join"

+    if program.sources is not None:

+        yield v14, "a sources block"

+    if program.scoped:

+        yield v14, "a with block"

+    if program.schemas:

+        yield v12, "a schema block"

+    if program.params:

+        yield v12, "a params block"

+    if program.calcs:

+        yield v12, "calc"

+    if program.window is not None and program.window.param is not None:

+        yield v12, "window(param(...))"

+    for item in program.aggregate.items:

+        if item.function == "count" and item.column is not None:

+            yield v13, "count(<column>)"

+    if program.name is not None:

+        yield v12, "a pipeline block"

+    for top in P.program_expressions(program):

+        for node in P.walk(top):

+            if isinstance(node, P.Param):

+                yield v12, "param()"

+            elif isinstance(node, P.Cast):

+                yield v12, "cast()"

+            elif isinstance(node, P.Call):

+                if node.name in ("lag", "lead"):

+                    yield v12, "%s()" % node.name

+                elif node.name == "coalesce":

+                    yield v13, "coalesce()"

+                elif not is_builtin_function(node.name):

+                    yield v14, "user-defined function %s()" % node.name

+"""Data-quality bookkeeping.

+

+Secret: how rejected rows are classified, which failure category a bad

+record maps to in strict mode, and the JSON Lines shape and ordering of the

+bad-records report.

+"""

+

+import json

+import math

+from datetime import datetime

+

+from .errors import ExecutionError, InputError, TypeCheckError

+

+PARSE_TYPE_MISMATCH = "PARSE_TYPE_MISMATCH"

+TIMESTAMP_PARSE_ERROR = "TIMESTAMP_PARSE_ERROR"

+RUNTIME_ERROR = "RUNTIME_ERROR"

+TYPE_ERROR = "TYPE_ERROR"

+MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD = "MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD"

+PARQUET_TYPE_MISMATCH = "PARQUET_TYPE_MISMATCH"

+

+_STRICT_ERRORS = {

+    PARSE_TYPE_MISMATCH: TypeCheckError,

+    TIMESTAMP_PARSE_ERROR: TypeCheckError,

+    RUNTIME_ERROR: ExecutionError,

+    TYPE_ERROR: TypeCheckError,

+    MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD: TypeCheckError,

+    PARQUET_TYPE_MISMATCH: TypeCheckError,

+}

+

+

+class Provenance:

+    """Where a row came from: file path, physical line (None for Parquet), row ordinal."""

+

+    __slots__ = ("file", "line", "row")

+

+    def __init__(self, file, line, row):

+        self.file = file

+        self.line = line

+        self.row = row

+

+    def describe(self):

+        if self.line is not None:

+            return "%s:%d" % (self.file, self.line)

+        if self.row is not None:

+            return "%s: row %d" % (self.file, self.row)

+        return self.file

+

+

+class BadRecord:

+    """One rejected row.

+

+    error: optional MtlError class raised for it in strict mode (defaults by

+    classification).

+    """

+

+    def __init__(self, provenance, classification, message, context=None, error=None):

+        self.provenance = provenance

+        self.classification = classification

+        self.message = message

+        self.context = context or {}

+        self.error = error or _STRICT_ERRORS[classification]

+

+    def sort_key(self):

+        p = self.provenance

+        line = p.line if p.line is not None else -1

+        return (p.file, line, p.row if p.row is not None else -1)

+

+    def as_json(self):

+        p = self.provenance

+        obj = {

+            "file": p.file,

+            "line": p.line,

+            "row": p.row,

+            "error": self.classification,

+            "message": self.message,

+            "context": _json_safe(self.context),

+        }

+        return json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False)

+

+

+def _json_safe(value):

+    if value is None or isinstance(value, (bool, int, str)):

+        return value

+    if isinstance(value, float):

+        return value if math.isfinite(value) else repr(value)

+    if isinstance(value, dict):

+        return {str(k): _json_safe(v) for k, v in value.items()}

+    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):

+        return [_json_safe(v) for v in value]

+    if isinstance(value, datetime):

+        return value.isoformat()

+    if isinstance(value, bytes):

+        return value.decode("utf-8", "replace")

+    return str(value)

+

+

+class BadRecordLog:

+    """Collects bad records; in strict mode the first one aborts the run."""

+

+    def __init__(self, strict):

+        self.strict = strict

+        self.records = []

+

+    def add(self, record):

+        self.records.append(record)

+        if self.strict:

+            raise record.error("%s: %s: %s" % (record.provenance.describe(),

+                                               record.classification, record.message))

+

+    def write(self, path):

+        """Write the JSON Lines report; nothing is created when there are no bad rows."""

+        if not path or not self.records:

+            return

+        ordered = sorted(self.records, key=BadRecord.sort_key)

+        text = "".join(r.as_json() + "\n" for r in ordered)

+        try:

+            with open(path, "wb") as handle:

+                handle.write(text.encode("utf-8"))

+        except OSError as exc:

+            raise InputError("cannot write bad records %r: %s" % (path, exc.strerror or exc))

+"""Failure categories.

+

+Secret: how failure categories map to exit codes and how the diagnostic

+and warning lines are formatted.

+"""

+

+

+class MtlError(Exception):

+    """Base class of all user-facing failures."""

+

+    _label = "runtime_error"

+    _code = 4

+

+

+class DslError(MtlError):

+    """The DSL program is syntactically or structurally invalid."""

+

+    _label = "bad_dsl"

+    _code = 1

+

+

+class TypeCheckError(MtlError):

+    """A value or expression has an unacceptable type."""

+

+    _label = "type_error"

+    _code = 2

+

+

+class InputError(MtlError):

+    """Inputs could not be read (files, CSV structure, CLI arguments)."""

+

+    _label = "bad_io"

+    _code = 3

+

+

+class ExecutionError(MtlError):

+    """Evaluation failed at run time (division by zero, non-finite values)."""

+

+    _label = "runtime_error"

+    _code = 4

+

+

+class ConfigError(MtlError):

+    """The ingest configuration is malformed or inconsistent with the DSL."""

+

+    _label = "config_error"

+    _code = 5

+

+

+class ArtifactError(MtlError):

+    """The DSL version is unsupported or the resumable state cannot be used."""

+

+    _label = "artifact_error"

+    _code = 6

+

+

+def report(error, stream):

+    """Write the one-line diagnostic for `error` and return its exit code."""

+    message = " ".join(str(error).split()) or error.__class__.__name__

+    stream.write("ERROR:%s:%s\n" % (error._label, message))

+    stream.flush()

+    return error._code

+

+

+def warn(category, message, stream):

+    """Write a one-line warning (the run still succeeds)."""

+    stream.write("WARNING:%s:%s\n" % (category, " ".join(message.split())))

+    stream.flush()

+"""Declarative multi-source ingestion.

+

+Secret: the ingest-config document (YAML or JSON) and its validation, how

+source patterns are expanded and files assigned to sources by precedence,

+and how each source's mapping (drop, rename, cast, defaults), schema

+conversion, required-field checks and schema calcs turn raw file rows into

+typed rows.

+"""

+

+import glob

+import json

+import math

+import os

+import re

+from collections import OrderedDict, namedtuple

+from datetime import date, datetime

+

+from . import inputs

+from . import quality as Q

+from . import sources as S

+from . import valuetypes as T

+from .declarations import resolve_named_schema

+from .dsl_parser import TYPE_NAMES

+from .errors import ConfigError, ExecutionError, InputError, MtlError, TypeCheckError

+from .expressions import cast_value, coerce, compile_expression, is_assignable

+from .timestamps import TimestampParser

+

+_SOURCE_NAME = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$")

+_MAPPING_KEYS = ("drop", "rename", "cast", "defaults")

+

+Defaults = namedtuple("Defaults", "tz timestamp_format nulls format recursive")

+

+SourceSpec = namedtuple("SourceSpec", "name patterns recursive format schema precedence "

+                                      "ts_parser nulls drop rename cast defaults required "

+                                      "base_dir")

+# patterns: path-or-glob strings; drop: tuple; rename/cast/defaults: OrderedDict;

+# defaults values are typed raw values (see _typed); required: tuple

+

+

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

+# The configuration document

+

+

+def load_config(path, defaults):

+    """Read and validate the ingest config; returns SourceSpecs in config order."""

+    try:

+        with open(path, "rb") as handle:

+            data = handle.read()

+    except OSError as exc:

+        raise InputError("cannot read ingest config %r: %s" % (path, exc.strerror or exc))

+    try:

+        text = data.decode("utf-8-sig")

+    except UnicodeDecodeError:

+        raise ConfigError("ingest config %r is not valid UTF-8" % path)

+    document = _parse_document(text, path)

+    if isinstance(document, dict):

+        if "sources" not in document:

+            raise ConfigError("ingest config has no 'sources' list")

+        entries = document["sources"]

+    else:

+        entries = document

+    if not isinstance(entries, list) or not entries:

+        raise ConfigError("ingest config 'sources' must be a non-empty list")

+    base_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))

+    specs = []

+    names = set()

+    for index, entry in enumerate(entries):

+        spec = _parse_source(index, entry, defaults, base_dir)

+        if spec.name in names:

+            raise ConfigError("source name %r is defined more than once" % spec.name)

+        names.add(spec.name)

+        specs.append(spec)

+    return specs

+

+

+def _parse_document(text, path):

+    if path.lower().endswith(".json"):

+        try:

+            return json.loads(text)

+        except ValueError as exc:

+            raise ConfigError("malformed JSON ingest config: %s" % exc)

+    try:

+        import yaml

+    except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - PyYAML is a declared dependency

+        try:

+            return json.loads(text)

+        except ValueError as exc:

+            raise ConfigError("malformed ingest config (PyYAML unavailable): %s" % exc)

+    try:

+        return yaml.safe_load(text)

+    except yaml.YAMLError as exc:

+        raise ConfigError("malformed YAML ingest config: %s" % " ".join(str(exc).split()))

+

+

+def _parse_source(index, entry, defaults, base_dir):

+    if not isinstance(entry, dict):

+        raise ConfigError("sources[%d] must be a mapping" % index)

+    name = entry.get("name")

+    if not isinstance(name, str) or not _SOURCE_NAME.match(name):

+def _nulls(value, fallback, where):

+    if value is None:

+        return fallback

+    if isinstance(value, str):

+        return frozenset(m.strip() for m in value.split(",") if m.strip() != "")

+    if not isinstance(value, list):

+        raise ConfigError("%s: 'nulls' must be a list of strings" % where)

+    markers = set()

+    for marker in value:

+        if marker is None:  # an unquoted YAML null / ~

+            markers.update(("null", "NULL", "Null", "~"))

+        elif isinstance(marker, bool):

+            markers.add("true" if marker else "false")

+        elif isinstance(marker, (str, int, float)):

+        else:

+    return frozenset(m for m in markers if m != "")

+

+def _names(value, where, what):

+    if value is None:

+        return []

+    if isinstance(value, str):

+        value = [value]

+    if not isinstance(value, list) or not all(isinstance(v, str) and v for v in value):

+        raise ConfigError("%s: %s must be a list of column names" % (where, what))

+    return value

+

+

+def _str_map(value, where, what):

+    if value is None:

+        return OrderedDict()

+    if not isinstance(value, dict):

+        raise ConfigError("%s: %s must be a mapping" % (where, what))

+    result = OrderedDict()

+    for key, target in value.items():

+        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key or not isinstance(target, str) or not target:

+            raise ConfigError("%s: %s must map column names to names" % (where, what))

+        result[key] = target

+    return result

+

+

+_INVALID = object()

+

+

+def _typed(value, ts_parser):

+    """A config scalar as a raw value (see _Raw), None for null, _INVALID otherwise."""

+    if value is None:

+        return None

+    if isinstance(value, bool):

+        return ("v", T.BOOL, value)

+    if isinstance(value, int):

+        return ("v", T.INT, value)

+    if isinstance(value, float):

+        if not math.isfinite(value):

+            return _INVALID

+        return ("v", T.FLOAT, value)

+    if isinstance(value, str):

+        return ("t", value)

+    if isinstance(value, datetime):

+        return ("v", T.TIMESTAMP, ts_parser.localize(value))

+    if isinstance(value, date):

+        return ("v", T.TIMESTAMP, ts_parser.localize(datetime(value.year, value.month,

+                                                              value.day)))

+    return _INVALID

+

+

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

+# File assignment

+

+

+def assign_files(specs):

+    """name -> files of that source (sorted by absolute path).

+

+    A file matched by several sources goes to the one with the lowest

+    precedence; equal lowest precedence is a configuration error.

+    """

+    matches = OrderedDict()   # realpath -> {source name: InputFile}

+    for spec in specs:

+        for pattern in spec.patterns:

+            for key, entry in _expand(spec, pattern).items():

+                matches.setdefault(key, OrderedDict()).setdefault(spec.name, entry)

+    by_name = {spec.name: spec for spec in specs}

+    assigned = OrderedDict((spec.name, []) for spec in specs)

+    for key, claims in matches.items():

+        best = min(by_name[n].precedence for n in claims)

+        winners = [n for n in claims if by_name[n].precedence == best]

+        if len(winners) > 1:

+            raise ConfigError("file %r matches sources %s with equal precedence %d"

+                              % (claims[winners[0]].path, ", ".join(repr(w) for w in winners),

+                                 best))

+        assigned[winners[0]].append(claims[winners[0]])

+    for name in assigned:

+        assigned[name].sort(key=lambda f: os.path.abspath(f.path))

+    return assigned

+

+

+def _expand(spec, pattern):

+    """Files of one pattern; relative patterns are tried against the working

+    directory first, then against the directory of the config file."""

+    pattern = os.path.expanduser(pattern)

+    candidates = [pattern]

+    if not os.path.isabs(pattern):

+        anchored = os.path.join(spec.base_dir, pattern)

+        if os.path.abspath(pattern) != os.path.normpath(anchored):

+            candidates.append(anchored)

+    for candidate in candidates:

+        if os.path.exists(candidate) or glob.has_magic(candidate):

+            found = inputs.expand(candidate, spec.format, spec.recursive)

+            if found:

+                return found

+    if not glob.has_magic(pattern) and not any(os.path.exists(c) for c in candidates):

+        raise InputError("source %r: input %r does not exist" % (spec.name, pattern))

+    return {}

+

+

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

+# Typed rows of one source

+#

+# Raw values flowing through the mapping are tuples:

+#   ("t", text)            a CSV/TSV cell

+#   ("p", kind, value)     a Parquet value of logical `kind`

+#   ("v", type, value)     an already typed value (after cast or from a default)

+

+

+class SourceReader:

+    """Static column types and (lazily) the typed rows of one configured source."""

+

+    def __init__(self, spec, schemas, fallback_schema, files):

+        self.spec = spec

+        self.files = files

+        self.rows_read = OrderedDict()   # file path -> records read from it

+        self._rows = None

+        self._mapped = None

+        self.defaults = spec.defaults

+        schema_name = spec.schema or fallback_schema

+        if spec.schema is not None and spec.schema not in schemas:

+            raise ConfigError("source %r uses schema %r, which the DSL does not define"

+                              % (spec.name, spec.schema))

+        self.schema = None if schema_name is None else resolve_named_schema(schemas,

+                                                                            schema_name)

+        if self.schema is not None:

+            self.physical = OrderedDict(self.schema.physical)

+            self._check_defaults()

+            fields = self.schema.fields

+            for name in spec.required:

+                if name not in fields:

+                    raise ConfigError("source %r: required field %r is not in schema %r"

+                                      % (spec.name, name, self.schema.name))

+            self.columns = OrderedDict((n, f.type) for n, f in fields.items())

+            self._calcs = self._compile_calcs()

+        else:

+            self.physical = None      # inferred from the data on first use

+            self.columns = None

+            self._calcs = []

+

+    # -- static -----------------------------------------------------------

+    def _check_defaults(self):

+        """Convert defaults of schema fields to the field types up front."""

+        self.defaults = OrderedDict()

+        for column, raw in self.spec.defaults.items():

+            col_type = self.physical.get(column)

+            if col_type is not None:

+                if col_type == T.STRING and raw[0] == "v" and raw[1] != T.TIMESTAMP:

+                    raw = ("t", _text_of(raw))

+                try:

+                    raw = ("v", col_type, _convert(raw, col_type, self._converter(column)))

+                except S._CellError:

+                    raise ConfigError("source %r: default for %r is not a valid %s"

+                                      % (self.spec.name, column, col_type))

+            self.defaults[column] = raw

+

+    def _compile_calcs(self):

+        names = _Types(self.physical)

+        compiled = []

+        for field in self.schema.calcs:

+            result = compile_expression(field.expression, names, ts_parser=self.spec.ts_parser)

+            if not is_assignable(field.type, result.type):

+                raise TypeCheckError("schema field %r is declared %s but its expression is %s"

+                                     % (field.name, field.type, result.type))

+            names.define(field.name, field.type)

+            compiled.append((field.name, coerce(field.type, result)))

+        return compiled

+

+    def _converter(self, column):

+        return S._Converter(self.physical[column], self.spec.nulls, self.spec.ts_parser)

+

+    def ensure_columns(self):

+        """Column types; schema-less sources infer them from their files."""

+        if self.columns is None:

+            self._load()

+        return self.columns

+

+    # -- rows -------------------------------------------------------------

+    def rows(self, log):

+        """List of (provenance, values) of the rows that survived validation."""

+        if self._rows is None:

+            mapped = self._load()

+            self._rows = self._convert_rows(mapped, log)

+        return self._rows

+

+    @property

+    def loaded(self):

+        return self._rows is not None

+

+    def max_timestamp(self):

+        """The latest `timestamp` among the rows that survived validation, or None."""

+        latest = None

+        for _, values in self._rows or ():

+            value = values.get("timestamp")

+            if isinstance(value, datetime) and (latest is None or value > latest):

+                latest = value

+        return latest

+

+    def _load(self):

+        if self._mapped is None:

+            mapped = []

+            for entry in self.files:

+                mapped.extend(self._read(entry))

+            self._mapped = mapped

+            if self.physical is None:

+                self._infer(mapped)

+        return self._mapped

+

+    def _read(self, entry):

+        table = S.read_file(entry)

+        if table.kind == "parquet":

+            table.load(set(table.columns), self.spec.ts_parser)

+        self.rows_read[table.path] = table.rows_read

+        if table.kind == "parquet":

+            columns = [(n,) + table.data[n] for n in table.columns if n in table.data]

+            for index in range(table.nrows):

+                prov = Q.Provenance(table.path, None, index + 1)

+                raw = OrderedDict((n, ("p", kind, values[index])) for n, kind, values in columns)

+                yield self._map(prov, raw)

+            return

+        header = table.columns

+        width = len(header)

+        for ordinal, (line, cells) in enumerate(table.rows, start=1):

+            prov = Q.Provenance(table.path, line, ordinal)

+            if len(cells) != width:

+                if len(cells) < width:

+                    classification = Q.MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD

+                    message = "record has %d fields, expected %d (missing: %s)" % (

+                        len(cells), width, ", ".join(header[len(cells):]))

+                else:

+                    classification = Q.PARSE_TYPE_MISMATCH

+                    message = "record has %d fields, expected %d" % (len(cells), width)

+                yield ("bad", Q.BadRecord(prov, classification, message,

+                                          {"fields": list(cells), "header": list(header)},

+                                          error=InputError))

+                continue

+            yield self._map(prov, OrderedDict((h, ("t", c)) for h, c in zip(header, cells)))

+

+    def _map(self, prov, raw):

+        """Apply drop, rename, cast and defaults, in that order."""

+        spec = self.spec

+        for column in spec.drop:

+            raw.pop(column, None)

+        if spec.rename:

+            renamed = OrderedDict()

+            targets = {spec.rename[c] for c in raw if c in spec.rename}

+            for column, value in raw.items():

+                if column not in spec.rename and column not in targets:

+                    renamed[column] = value

+            for column, value in raw.items():

+                if column in spec.rename:

+                    renamed[spec.rename[column]] = value

+            raw = renamed

+        for column, target in spec.cast.items():

+            if column not in raw:

+                continue

+            try:

+                raw[column] = ("v", target, self._cast(raw[column], target))

+            except S._CellError as err:

+                return ("bad", Q.BadRecord(prov, err.classification,

+                                           "column %r: cast to %s failed: %s"

+                                           % (column, target, err.message),

+                                           {"column": column, "value": _show(raw[column]),

+                                            "cast": target}))

+        for column, value in self.defaults.items():

+            if column not in raw or self._is_null(raw[column]):

+                raw[column] = value

+        return ("row", prov, raw)

+

+    def _is_null(self, raw):

+        if raw[0] == "t":

+            return raw[1] == "" or raw[1].strip() in self.spec.nulls

+        value = raw[2]

+        return value is None or (isinstance(value, float) and math.isnan(value))

+

+    def _cast(self, raw, target):

+        if self._is_null(raw):

+            return None

+        converter = S._Converter(target, self.spec.nulls, self.spec.ts_parser)

+        if raw[0] == "t":

+            return converter.text(raw[1])

+        if raw[0] == "p":

+            kind, value = raw[1], raw[2]

+            if kind == "string":

+                return converter.text(value)

+            if kind == "binary":

+                return converter.text(bytes(value).decode("utf-8", "replace"))

+            if kind == "date":

+                source = T.TIMESTAMP

+                value = self.spec.ts_parser.localize(datetime(value.year, value.month,

+                                                              value.day))

+            elif kind == "decimal":

+                source, value = T.FLOAT, float(value)

+            elif kind in ("int", "float", "bool") or (kind == "timestamp"

+                                                      and isinstance(value, datetime)):

+                source = S._KIND_TYPES[kind]

+            else:

+                raise S._CellError(Q.PARQUET_TYPE_MISMATCH, "Parquet %s value %s cannot be "

+                                   "cast to %s" % (kind, _show(raw), target))

+        else:

+            source, value = raw[1], raw[2]

+        try:

+            return cast_value(value, source, target, self.spec.ts_parser)

+        except (TypeCheckError, ExecutionError, ValueError, OverflowError) as exc:

+            raise S._CellError(Q.PARSE_TYPE_MISMATCH, "%s value %s cannot be cast to %s (%s)"

+                               % (source, _show(raw), target, exc))

+

+    def _infer(self, mapped):

+        """Column types of a schema-less source (fixed event columns + inferred extras)."""

+        seen = OrderedDict()

+        for item in mapped:

+            if item[0] == "row":

+                for column, raw in item[2].items():

+                    seen.setdefault(column, []).append(raw)

+        types = OrderedDict(S.KNOWN)

+        for column, raws in seen.items():

+            if column in types:

+                continue

+            typed = {r[1] for r in raws if r[0] == "v" and r[2] is not None}

+            kinds = {r[1] for r in raws if r[0] == "p" and r[2] is not None

+                     and r[1] != "null"}

+            cells = [r[1] for r in raws if r[0] == "t"]

+            mapped_types = typed | {S._KIND_TYPES[k] for k in kinds}

+            if not cells and mapped_types:

+                if len(mapped_types) == 1:

+                    types[column] = mapped_types.pop()

+                    continue

+                if mapped_types == {T.INT, T.FLOAT}:

+                    types[column] = T.FLOAT

+                    continue

+            cells.extend(_text_of(r) for r in raws if r[0] != "t" and r[-1] is not None)

+            types[column] = S._infer_text(cells, self.spec.nulls, self.spec.ts_parser)

+        for column, target in self.spec.cast.items():

+            if column in types:

+                types[column] = target

+        self.physical = types

+        self.columns = OrderedDict(types)

+

+    def _convert_rows(self, mapped, log):

+        rows = []

+        physical = self.physical

+        converters = {n: self._converter(n) for n in physical}

+        required = self.spec.required

+        for item in mapped:

+            if item[0] == "bad":

+                log.add(item[1])

+                continue

+            prov, raw = item[1], item[2]

+            values = OrderedDict()

+            failure = None

+            for name, col_type in physical.items():

+                value = raw.get(name)

+                try:

+                    values[name] = None if value is None else _convert(value, col_type,

+                                                                      converters[name])

+                except S._CellError as err:

+                    failure = Q.BadRecord(prov, err.classification,

+                                          "column %r: %s" % (name, err.message),

+                                          {"column": name, "value": _show(value),

+                                           "expected_type": col_type})

+                    break

+            if failure is None:

+                failure = self._missing(prov, values, required, physical)

+            if failure is None:

+                try:

+                    for name, evaluate in self._calcs:

+                        values[name] = evaluate(_Record(values))

+                except (ExecutionError, TypeCheckError, ArithmeticError, ValueError) as exc:

+                    failure = Q.BadRecord(prov, Q.RUNTIME_ERROR, str(exc), {"values": values})

+            if failure is None:

+                failure = self._missing(prov, values, required, None)

+            if failure is not None:

+                log.add(failure)

+                continue

+            rows.append((prov, values))

+        return rows

+

+    def _missing(self, prov, values, required, among):

+        for name in required:

+            if (among is None or name in among) and values.get(name) is None:

+                return Q.BadRecord(prov, Q.MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD,

+                                   "required field %r is null" % name,

+                                   {"column": name, "source": self.spec.name,

+                                    "values": dict(values)})

+        return None

+

+

+def _convert(raw, col_type, converter):

+    """Schema conversion of one mapped raw value; raises sources._CellError."""

+    tag = raw[0]

+    if tag == "t":

+        return converter.text(raw[1])

+    if tag == "p":

+        return converter.parquet(raw[1], raw[2])

+    value_type, value = raw[1], raw[2]

+    if value is None:

+        return None

+    if value_type == col_type:

+        return value

+    if value_type == T.INT and col_type == T.FLOAT:

+        return float(value)

+    if value_type == T.STRING and col_type != T.STRING:

+        return converter.text(value)

+    raise S._CellError(Q.PARSE_TYPE_MISMATCH, "%s value %s does not conform to schema type %s"

+                       % (value_type, _show(raw), col_type))

+

+

+def _text_of(raw):

+    if raw[0] == "p":

+        return S._canonical_text(raw[1], raw[2])

+    value = raw[2]

+    if isinstance(value, bool):

+        return "true" if value else "false"

+    if isinstance(value, datetime):

+        from .timestamps import format_utc

+        return format_utc(value)

+    return repr(value) if isinstance(value, float) else str(value)

+

+

+def _show(raw):

+    if raw is None:

+        return None

+    value = raw[-1]

+    if isinstance(value, (datetime, date)):

+        return str(value)

+    return value

+

+

+class _Types:

+    def __init__(self, types):

+        self._types = OrderedDict(types)

+

+    def has(self, name):

+        return name in self._types

+

+    def type_of(self, name):

+        return self._types[name]

+

+    def define(self, name, value_type):

+        self._types[name] = value_type

+

+

+class _Record:

+    __slots__ = ("data",)

+

+    def __init__(self, data):

+        self.data = data

+

+    def get(self, name):

+        return self.data.get(name)

+"""Schema and parameter declarations.

+

+Secret: how schema inheritance is resolved (field order, override rules,

+cycle and forward-reference detection, evaluation order of calculated

+fields) and how parameter values are bound from defaults and CLI text.

+"""

+

+import math

+import re

+from collections import OrderedDict, namedtuple

+

+from . import valuetypes as T

+from .errors import DslError, TypeCheckError

+from .expressions import column_references, uses_row_relative

+

+ResolvedSchema = namedtuple("ResolvedSchema", "name fields physical calcs")

+# fields:   OrderedDict name -> FieldDef (final definition of every field)

+# physical: OrderedDict name -> type of the fields read from the CSV

+# calcs:    FieldDefs of calculated fields, in a dependency-respecting order

+

+_INT_TEXT = re.compile(r"^\s*[+-]?\d+\s*$")

+_FLOAT_TEXT = re.compile(r"^\s*[+-]?(\d+\.?\d*([eE][+-]?\d+)?|\.\d+([eE][+-]?\d+)?)\s*$")

+

+

+def _legal_override(old, new):

+    return old == new or (old == T.INT and new == T.FLOAT)

+

+

+def resolve_schema(program):

+    """Resolve the schema named by the pipeline's `using`; None for bare programs."""

+    if program.schema_name is None:

+        return None

+    return resolve_named_schema(program.schemas, program.schema_name)

+

+

+def resolve_named_schema(schemas, schema_name):

+    """Resolve schema `schema_name` (with its inheritance chain) from `schemas`."""

+    chain = []

+    seen = set()

+    name = schema_name

+    while name is not None:

+        if name in seen:

+            raise DslError("circular schema inheritance involving %r" % name)

+        if name not in schemas:

+            raise DslError("schema %r extends unknown schema %r" % (chain[-1].name, name))

+        seen.add(name)

+        chain.append(schemas[name])

+        name = schemas[name].base

+    _check_all_cycles(schemas)

+

+    fields = OrderedDict()

+    for schema in reversed(chain):

+        for field in schema.fields:

+            if field.expression is not None:

+                if uses_row_relative(field.expression):

+                    raise DslError("schema %r field %r: lag()/lead() are not allowed in schemas"

+                                   % (schema.name, field.name))

+                for ref in column_references(field.expression):

+                    if ref not in fields:

+                        raise DslError("schema %r field %r references unknown or later field %r"

+                                       % (schema.name, field.name, ref))

+            if field.name in fields:

+                old = fields[field.name].type

+                if not _legal_override(old, field.type):

+                    raise TypeCheckError("schema %r cannot override field %r from %s to %s"

+                                         % (schema.name, field.name, old, field.type))

+            fields[field.name] = field

+

+    physical = OrderedDict((f.name, f.type) for f in fields.values() if f.expression is None)

+    return ResolvedSchema(schema_name, fields, physical, _calc_order(fields))

+

+

+def _check_all_cycles(schemas):

+    for start in schemas:

+        seen = set()

+        name = start

+        while name is not None and name in schemas:

+            if name in seen:

+                raise DslError("circular schema inheritance involving %r" % name)

+            seen.add(name)

+            name = schemas[name].base

+        if name is not None:

+            raise DslError("schema %r extends unknown schema %r" % (start, name))

+

+

+def _calc_order(fields):

+    order = []

+    state = {}

+

+    def visit(name):

+        if state.get(name) == "done":

+            return

+        if state.get(name) == "active":

+            raise DslError("calculated field %r depends on itself" % name)

+        state[name] = "active"

+        field = fields[name]

+        for ref in column_references(field.expression):

+            if ref in fields and fields[ref].expression is not None:

+                visit(ref)

+        state[name] = "done"

+        order.append(field)

+

+    for name, field in fields.items():

+        if field.expression is not None:

+            visit(name)

+    return order

+

+

+def parse_cli_params(pairs):

+    """Turn 'key=value' strings into a dict (last one wins); None on bad syntax."""

+    values = {}

+    for pair in pairs:

+        key, sep, value = pair.partition("=")

+        key = key.strip()

+        if not sep or not re.match(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$", key):

+            return None

+        values[key] = value

+    return values

+

+

+def bind_params(program, cli_values, ts_parser):

+    """Return name -> (type, value) for every declared parameter.

+

+    Bare programs (no pipeline block) expose CLI values as strings.

+    """

+    if program.name is None and not program.params:

+        return {k: (T.STRING, v) for k, v in cli_values.items()}

+    bound = {}

+    for decl in program.params:

+        value_type = decl.type

+        default = decl.default

+        if value_type is None:

+            value_type = default.kind if default is not None else T.STRING

+        if decl.name in cli_values:

+            text = cli_values[decl.name]

+            try:

+                value = _parse_text(text, value_type, ts_parser)

+            except (ValueError, OverflowError):

+                raise TypeCheckError("parameter %r value %r is not a valid %s"

+                                     % (decl.name, text, value_type))

+        elif default is not None:

+            value = _default_value(decl.name, default, value_type, ts_parser)

+        else:

+            raise DslError("parameter %r has no default and was not given with --param"

+                           % decl.name)

+        bound[decl.name] = (value_type, value)

+    return bound

+

+

+def _default_value(name, literal, value_type, ts_parser):

+    kind, value = literal.kind, literal.value

+    if kind == value_type:

+        if isinstance(value, float) and not math.isfinite(value):

+            raise TypeCheckError("parameter %r default is not finite" % name)

+        return value

+    if value_type == T.FLOAT and kind == T.INT:

+        return float(value)

+    if value_type == T.TIMESTAMP and kind == T.STRING:

+        try:

+            return ts_parser.parse(value)

+        except (ValueError, OverflowError):

+            pass

+    raise TypeCheckError("parameter %r default %r is not a valid %s" % (name, value, value_type))

+

+

+def _parse_text(text, value_type, ts_parser):

+    if value_type == T.STRING:

+        return text

+    if value_type == T.INT:

+        if not _INT_TEXT.match(text):

+            raise ValueError(text)

+        return int(text)

+    if value_type == T.FLOAT:

+        if not _FLOAT_TEXT.match(text):

+            raise ValueError(text)

+        value = float(text)

+        if not math.isfinite(value):

+            raise ValueError(text)

+        return value

+    if value_type == T.BOOL:

+        lowered = text.strip().lower()

+        if lowered not in ("true", "false"):

+            raise ValueError(text)

+        return lowered == "true"

+    return ts_parser.parse(text)

+"""User-defined functions.

+

+Secret: how --udf files are loaded and how their functions register (the

+@udf decorator, a UDFS table, a register(registry) hook, or plain annotated

+functions), signature validation, and how a call converts arguments,

+propagates nulls, checks results and wraps failures.

+

+A UDF file is Python.  Any of these registers `score(float, float) -> float`:

+

+    @udf(args=["float", "float"], returns="float")

+    def score(a, b): ...

+

+    @udf

+    def score(a: float, b: float) -> float: ...

+

+    UDFS = {"score": {"fn": score, "args": ["float", "float"], "returns": "float"}}

+

+    def register(registry):

+        registry.register("score", score, args=["float", "float"], returns="float")

+

+Without any explicit registration, every public, fully annotated function

+defined in the file is registered.

+"""

+import hashlib

+import inspect

+import math

+import re

+import sys

+import types

+from collections import OrderedDict

+from datetime import datetime, timezone

+

+from . import valuetypes as T

+from .dsl_parser import AGGREGATE_FUNCTIONS, is_builtin_function

+from .errors import ConfigError, ExecutionError, InputError

+_RESERVED = ("param", "cast", "true", "false", "in", "as") + AGGREGATE_FUNCTIONS

+_TYPE_NAMES = {

+    "float": T.FLOAT, "double": T.FLOAT, "int": T.INT, "integer": T.INT,

+    "string": T.STRING, "str": T.STRING, "bool": T.BOOL, "boolean": T.BOOL,

+    "timestamp": T.TIMESTAMP, "datetime": T.TIMESTAMP, "datetime.datetime": T.TIMESTAMP,
